help.document kept-edits:
Usage: dohc document kept-edits [options]

List live documents whose edits the server refused, and where dohc keeps those edits.

storedOn is this-computer, or server for a document the server hosts.
A recovery of paused means the edits wait for you. Save a recovery copy, or try
again. A new refusal changes the incident.
When saveOnly is true, save a recovery copy instead. If recovery is unreadable,
retry reads the edits again.
A recovery of not-written or stopping means a Stop kept the edits. Run
stop-again to finish it.
A recovery of cannot-write means only a recovery copy can return the edits.
Copied means a recovery copy of edits the server keeps is saved.
If the server accepts a later edit to the document, copied returns to paused.
Save another recovery copy to include that edit.
A recovery of unreadable means dohc could not read the edits it keeps on this
computer, and reason says why. Run retry-kept-edits to read them again.
earlier is true when the server keeps the edits in an earlier copy of the
workspace. Save a recovery copy to get them back; try again cannot reach them.

help.document save-recovery-copy:
Usage: dohc document save-recovery-copy <path> [<incident>] [options]

Save a document's kept edits next to it.

Accepts every recovery but unreadable.
With an incident from kept-edits, dohc saves exactly those kept edits. Without
one, it saves edits a Stop could not write first.
dohc writes a recovery package with every kept edit, and a readable copy when it
can read the edits as a document.
For edits the server keeps, dohc then tells the server the copy is saved, and
the recovery becomes copied.
keptEdits is kept when the edits stay where storedOn says, and copied when the
server may now release them.
It is ended for edits a Stop could not write: dohc no longer keeps them, and the
copy holds them.
dohc writes these files itself, not as the agent that asked.

Usage: dohc document retry-kept-edits <path> <incident> [options]

Send a document's kept edits to the server once more.

Take the incident from kept-edits. Accepts a recovery of paused, or copied for
edits the server keeps.
For unreadable, dohc reads the kept edits again. It fails with the reason while
it still cannot read them.
A not-written or stopping document needs stop-again instead.
Run kept-edits again to follow it: retrying until the server answers, paused
with a new incident if it refuses again.

help.document stop-again:
Usage: dohc document stop-again <path> <incident> [options]

Stop live editing again for a document whose Stop kept its edits.

Take the incident from kept-edits. Accepts a recovery of not-written or
stopping.
For not-written, dohc writes the kept edits into the file. For stopping, it asks
the server again to stop live editing.
keptEdits is recovered once the file holds the edits, kept while dohc still
keeps them, and none when it kept none.
dohc refuses while the document is open in an editor. Run kept-edits again to
follow it.

help.account delete:
Usage: dohc account delete [options]

Delete the connected server account and the workspaces it owns on the server.

dohc reads the account password from stdin, or asks for it when stdin is a
terminal. Never pass it as an argument.
This cannot be undone. Copies on this computer stay. People you shared with lose
access and keep their copies.
If you create an account again later, the server will not accept your old copies
of the deleted workspaces. Its backups keep the data until they expire.
When the server cannot finish at once, the account stays blocked and the server
finishes later. Either way, the dohc app disconnects from the server. If it
cannot, delete exits 1 and says how to finish.
If the preview expired or changed, run deletePreview again.

Run dohc inside a workspace folder while the dohc app is open.
Unlike other commands, account verbs also work outside a workspace folder.

Options:
  --server <address>        Use server from deletePreview. Required.
  --preview-token <token>   Use previewToken from deletePreview. Required.
  --as-agent                Post and read chat as an agent.
  --json                    Print the result as JSON.
  --help                    Show help. -h does the same.
